scope_of_review: RE-REVIEW limited to the r1 blocker (OQ1 missing-barrier soundness) + the r1 non-blocking OQ2 clarification, plus a no-regression check that r2 changed ONLY A.4.1 + the error-variant usage + AT-1606 + A.4.2 + AT-1635/1636 and left the 4 CRITICAL fixes / relabel / coopmat-from-shared intact.
oq1_soundness_status:
STILL UNSOUND — a NARROWER, but REAL, false positive survives r2. The r2 rule fixed the original same-INDEX self-read false positive (`tile[i]=v; ...=tile[i];` now ProvablyEqual -> NO diagnostic; correctly excluded; AT-1636 locks it). BUT the rule pairs the read against ONLY the MOST-RECENT SharedWrite of the id (A.4.1 + typecheck.rs change item both say 'let S[w] be the MOST-RECENT SharedWrite ... and S[r] a later SharedRead of the SAME id'). The 'same-invocation-different-slot' case the review prompt asked to probe is therefore mis-handled: a CORRECT straight-line kernel that writes TWO of ITS OWN slots and then reads back the FIRST one it wrote is hard-errored. Concrete counterexample (correct, needs NO barrier, yet HARD-ERRORED):
    tile[0u32] = a;      // write S[0] (this invocation's own slot)
    tile[1u32] = b;      // write S[1] -> now the MOST-RECENT write of `tile`
    let w = tile[0u32];  // read S[0] — this invocation's OWN earlier write, program-order-visible, NO barrier needed
  index_relation(most_recent_write=IntLit(1), read=IntLit(0)) = ProvablyDisequal (distinct constants) -> HARD ERROR SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead. This is a FALSE POSITIVE on a correct kernel: slot 0 WAS written by THIS invocation earlier in the same straight-line block, so the read is a safe same-invocation self-RAW, not a cross-invocation access. The architect's explicit soundness property ('the hard error fires on NO correct kernel') is NOT met. The defect is the same CLASS the prompt flagged (same-invocation-multi-slot), just shifted: r1 missed same-index; r2 fixes same-index but still mis-classifies same-invocation-EARLIER-slot because it forgets all writes except the most-recent.
oq1_single_invocation_workgroup_analysis: ACCEPTABLE (NOT a false positive). A @workgroup(1,1,1) kernel that writes S[0] and reads S[1] (distinct constants -> ProvablyDisequal -> HARD ERROR) is NOT a correct kernel being falsely rejected: with a single invocation, S[1] was written by NOBODY (this invocation wrote only S[0]; there are no other invocations), so the read is an UNINITIALIZED Workgroup read — buggy REGARDLESS of any barrier (the spec itself documents 'reading a cell never written reads garbage'). A barrier would not make it correct. The hard error therefore rejects an already-incorrect kernel, preserving the 'fires on no correct kernel' property. The only blemish is a MISLEADING diagnostic NAME ('missing barrier before cross-invocation read' when the true bug is an uninitialized read) — cosmetic, not a soundness hole. Note the spec does NOT condition the analysis on workgroup size, and it does not need to: the rule is sound for the single-invocation case as-is. Conditioning on workgroup_size==1 to SUPPRESS the error would be WRONG (it would let the uninitialized read through silently).
oq1_same_invocation_multislot_analysis: THIS is the residual false positive (see oq1_soundness_status). Distinguish two sub-cases the prompt raised: (1) invocation writes S[0], reads S[1] that ANOTHER invocation was supposed to write -> a barrier IS needed -> ProvablyDisequal -> HARD ERROR is CORRECT (genuine cross-invocation trap). (2) invocation writes S[0] AND S[1] (its own two slots), then reads back S[0] -> NO barrier needed (self-RAW on a slot it wrote) -> but ProvablyDisequal-vs-most-recent-write -> HARD ERROR is a FALSE POSITIVE. The analysis cannot tell (1) from (2) because it only remembers the most-recent write, not the SET of slots this invocation wrote in the block. FIX (must be specified before coding): before hard-erroring a ProvablyDisequal (write S[w], read S[r]), the analysis must also check whether `r` is ProvablyEqual to ANY EARLIER same-block SharedWrite index to the same id with no intervening barrier; if so, the read slot was written by THIS invocation -> NO error (safe self-read). Equivalently: track the SET of provably-written slots (constant indices + same-SSA-binding indices) since the last barrier, and hard-error ONLY when the read index is ProvablyDisequal to EVERY write in that set (i.e. provably a slot this invocation never wrote). If that set-membership is undecidable for the read index (dynamic/arith), DEMOTE to the advisory warning. This keeps the hard error sound (fires only when the read provably hits a slot THIS invocation never wrote — the true cross-invocation case) while preserving the zero-false-positive guarantee. Conservative acceptable alternative: if the architect does not want set-tracking, DEMOTE the entire ProvablyDisequal-most-recent-write case to the advisory warning (keeping only the cleanest single-write/single-read provable-cross-slot pattern as a hard error, or dropping the hard error to a warning altogether) — that also restores soundness, at the cost of weaker in-CI protection. EITHER fix is acceptable; the as-written most-recent-write-only rule is NOT.
oq2_status: RESOLVED as a MECHANISM, with ONE unflagged test regression. The new dedicated `conditional_depth` counter (incremented ONLY at if-then 956 / else 965, NOT at while 1174 nor for-range) is the correct discriminator and IS implementable against the verified code: divergent_context_depth (decl 545) increments at 956/965/1174; check_for_stmt (998) pushes only loop_stack (1124) and never touches divergent depth; check_while_stmt (1146) increments at 1174. So conditional_depth>0 fires for if/else bodies, stays 0 for for-range AND while bodies. The shipped K-loops are for-range (matmul_tile.axc / q4km_dequant_matmul.axc) -> conditional_depth 0 -> never flagged. while-body barrier permitted (AT-1635 second half holds). divergent_context_depth left to gate the subgroup-collective warning at 2089 — unchanged. The MECHANISM is sound. HOWEVER: the OQ2 hard error REGRESSES an EXISTING passing test that the r2 spec does NOT enumerate (see regression_found).
regression_found: REGRESSION (OQ2, unflagged): crates/axc-hir/src/typecheck.rs:4393-4405 `warn_barrier_in_if_body_no_warning` (AT-429) compiles `let p: bool = true; if p { workgroup_barrier(); } return;` and asserts `errors.is_empty()`. The NEW HirError::BarrierInDivergentContext keyed on `conditional_depth > 0` will FIRE for exactly this kernel (barrier inside an if-then body) -> errors NON-empty -> this existing test FAILS. The semantics change is itself CORRECT (a barrier in a divergent if-body is genuine Vulkan UB and SHOULD now be a hard error), but the r2 spec does not enumerate this test as a required edit. This is the SAME class of omission the r1 review forced the architect to fix for the metadata v2->v3 bump (enumerate EVERY existing assertion the new rule breaks). The architect MUST add typecheck.rs:4393 (AT-429) to files_to_modify: the test must be RESTRUCTURED — either (a) assert the kernel now PRODUCES BarrierInDivergentContext (the new correct behavior), renaming it e.g. error_barrier_in_if_body_is_BarrierInDivergentContext, or (b) move the barrier OUT of the if-body so it still validates the no-spurious-subgroup-warning property AT-429 originally protected. AT-1611's additive-only guarantee covers SPIR-V/API/bench-ids and was already scoped to EXCLUDE the metadata version literals; it must now ALSO acknowledge this OQ2 test-literal edit (the barrier-in-divergent semantics change is the intended event, not a regression — but the test edit must be explicitly mandated so the Coder performs it). No OTHER existing test or example places a barrier inside an if/else body (workspace grep: AT-429 line 4397 is the only barrier-in-conditional site; no example kernel does).

implementability_verified: CONFIRMED against crates/axc-hir/src/expr.rs. BindingId(pub u32) derives PartialEq/Eq/Hash (expr.rs:20-21). HirExprKind::IntLit{ value: IntLiteralValue } (expr.rs:94), LocalRead(BindingId) (expr.rs:97), GidBuiltin{ axis: u32 } (expr.rs:130) all exist as leaf forms, so index_relation's ProvablyEqual/ProvablyDisequal leaf cases (BindingId Eq, IntLit value equality, GidBuiltin axis equality) ARE decidable as claimed. HirStmt::Assign{ binding: BindingId, .. } (expr.rs:236) exists, so the 'no intervening reassignment of the binding' guard for the LocalRead-equal case is implementable. The PROPOSED FIX (set of prior-written slots since last barrier) is ALSO implementable with the same leaf machinery — it just requires remembering ALL same-block writes (constant + same-binding indices) since the last barrier, not only the most-recent, which is a Vec/SmallVec instead of a single Option. No new HIR data is needed. The OQ2 conditional_depth counter is implementable (verified the 956/965/998/1124/1146/1174/2008/2030/2089 sites all match the spec exactly).
critical_issues: CRITICAL (OQ1 — analysis STILL UNSOUND, blocks coding): the missing-barrier HARD ERROR pairs the read against ONLY the MOST-RECENT SharedWrite of the id. A correct straight-line kernel that writes two of its OWN slots and reads back the FIRST (`tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];`) is classified ProvablyDisequal (read 0 vs most-recent-write 1) -> HARD ERROR, a FALSE POSITIVE on a correct same-invocation self-read. The hard error must fire ONLY when the read index is provably disequal to EVERY prior same-block write index (since the last barrier) to that id — i.e. provably a slot THIS invocation never wrote (the true cross-invocation trap); otherwise NO error (if the read slot was provably written earlier by this invocation) or advisory warning (if undecidable). As specified, the soundness property 'fires on no correct kernel' is NOT met.

summary: RE-REVIEW (r2) of the M3.2 design, scoped to the r1 blocker (OQ1 soundness) + the OQ2 clarification + a no-regression check. The 4 CRITICAL fixes, the C1-not-FA2 relabel, and the coopmat-from-Workgroup-storage permission are ALL intact and unchanged from the r1-verified state — r2 touched only the claimed OQ1/OQ2 surface (A.4.1, A.4.2, the typecheck.rs change item, AT-1606/1635/1636, the benign error.rs:330 wording softening). OQ2's mechanism is RESOLVED and implementable: the dedicated conditional_depth counter (if/else-only, verified against typecheck.rs:956/965/998/1146/1174) correctly distinguishes conditional divergence from for-range AND while loop bodies, so the shipped for-range K-loops stay depth 0 (never flagged) and uniform while-body barriers are permitted (AT-1635 holds). BUT TWO defects block APPROVE. (1) BLOCKER — OQ1 is STILL UNSOUND: r2 fixed the original same-INDEX self-read false positive, but the rule pairs the read against ONLY the MOST-RECENT write of the id, so a CORRECT same-invocation kernel that writes two of its OWN slots and reads back the first (`tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];`) is mis-classified ProvablyDisequal -> HARD ERROR, a false positive on a correct kernel. The architect's explicit 'fires on no correct kernel' property is not met. The single-invocation-workgroup case (write S[0]/read S[1]) is, by contrast, ACCEPTABLE — that read is an uninitialized read, buggy regardless of barriers, so hard-erroring it rejects an already-incorrect kernel (only the diagnostic name is misleading). The fix: hard-error only when the read index is provably disequal to EVERY prior same-block write index since the last barrier (track the SET of written slots), demoting undecidable membership to the advisory warning — OR conservatively demote the whole most-recent-disequal case to the warning. Implementable with the same expr.rs leaf machinery (BindingId Eq / IntLit value / GidBuiltin axis, all VERIFIED present). (2) NON-BLOCKING-BUT-MUST-MANDATE — the OQ2 BarrierInDivergentContext hard error REGRESSES the existing passing test typecheck.rs:4393 (AT-429, `if p { workgroup_barrier(); }` asserts errors empty); the new behavior is correct but the r2 spec does not enumerate this test edit (the same class of omission r1 forced fixed for the metadata bump). NEEDS_REVISION: re-key the OQ1 hard error onto the full set of prior writes (restore zero false positives for the multi-slot self-read), and add the AT-429 test edit to files_to_modify. Both fixes are small and local; no architectural change.
